# Wealth Delta Tax

## What is the Wealth Delta Tax?

The **Wealth Delta Tax (WDT)** is a proposed alternative to conventional wealth taxation. Rather than taxing a snapshot of total wealth at a point in time, the WDT taxes the *change* in individual net wealth over a period — the delta — on an accrual basis, above an exemption threshold.

It has three defining features:

- **Accrual basis** — tax is assessed annually on the change in net worth, whether or not assets are sold
- **Symmetric loss refunds** — when net wealth falls, the taxpayer receives a refund at the same rate, eliminating the asymmetric treatment that makes conventional wealth taxes punitive in downturns
- **Sovereign Wealth Fund** — revenues flow into a pre-funded SWF with constitutional constraints on drawdown, separating fiscal policy from electoral cycles

This design directly addresses the three core objections to conventional wealth taxes: valuation uncertainty, liquidity pressure on illiquid asset holders, and the asymmetric gain/loss treatment that discourages risk-taking.

## How is the WDT different from a wealth tax?

A conventional wealth tax levies a charge on total net worth each year. This creates liquidity problems (you may owe tax on illiquid assets), valuation problems (private businesses and real assets are hard to value annually), and asymmetry problems (you pay tax when wealth rises but get nothing back when it falls).

The WDT addresses all three:

| Problem | Conventional wealth tax | Wealth Delta Tax |
|---|---|---|
| Liquidity | Tax on total stock; can force asset sales | Tax only on the *increase*; smaller base |
| Valuation | Full portfolio valued annually | Delta valued annually; errors partially cancel |
| Asymmetry | Gains taxed; losses ignored | Gains taxed; losses refunded symmetrically |

For a full comparison, see the [White Paper](wp.html).

## About this project

The WDT is designed for developed capitalist democracies. Its governing objective is to redesign the fiscal relationship between concentrated private wealth and democratic society — preserving productive dynamism while progressively reducing the tax burden on ordinary households.

The project is authored by K. Ogata and currently comprises 24 working papers covering the complete architecture of the proposal: mechanism design, moral foundations, valuation methodology, corporate and governance structures, revenue modelling, behavioural robustness, political architecture, and strategic adoption dynamics.

All papers are pre-peer review working papers and represent work in progress. The full series is also available for download at [Zenodo](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21964119) (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21964119).

## Where to start

- **New to the WDT?** Begin with the [White Paper (WP)](wp.html) for the full mechanism overview.
- **Want the normative case first?** [Moral Foundations (MF)](mf.html) develops the philosophical basis independently of the mechanism.
- **Interested in implementation?** [UK Jurisdiction (JUR)](jur.html) and [Phase One (PHASE1)](phase1.html) cover the practical pathway.
- **Interested in revenue?** [Rates and Revenue (RATES)](rates.html) and [Parameter Sweeps (SWEEPS)](sweeps.html) cover the fiscal modelling.
- **Returning reader?** Use the sidebar to navigate directly to the paper you want.
